question: International Tiger Day is observed on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is July 29th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• International Tiger Day (also called Global Tiger Day) is observed annually on 29 July. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय बाघ दिवस — 29 जुलाई)

 

• It was established in 2010 at the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit, where tiger range countries pledged the "Tx2" goal — to double the world's wild tiger population by 2022.

 

• The day aims to raise awareness about tiger conservation and promote habitat protection worldwide.

 

• India, home to over 70% of the world's wild tiger population, marks the day prominently; Project Tiger was launched in India in 1973.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's quadrennial All India Tiger Estimation report ("Status of Tigers in India") is released by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).

 

• Other related observances include World Wildlife Day (3 March) and World Environment Day (5 June).

 

NOTE

 

• July 5th (Option 1): No major tiger-conservation observance is marked on this date.

 

• July 30th (Option 2): Not the designated date; commonly confused with the actual date of 29 July.

 

• July 4th (Option 4): This is the United States' Independence Day and has no connection to tiger conservation.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to make the contents of a cell underlined in MS-Excel 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Excel (including Excel 365), Ctrl + 4 is the shortcut key to apply or remove underline formatting on the selected cell's contents.

 

• This is part of a consistent numeric-key formatting series: Ctrl+1 opens the Format Cells dialog box, Ctrl+2 toggles Bold, Ctrl+3 toggles Italic, Ctrl+4 toggles Underline, and Ctrl+5 toggles Strikethrough.

 

• These work alongside the more commonly known shortcuts Ctrl+B (Bold), Ctrl+I (Italic), and Ctrl+U (Underline).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl+1 (Format Cells) is one of Excel's most versatile shortcuts, giving quick access to number formats, alignment, borders and fill options.

 

• Ctrl+9 hides selected rows and Ctrl+0 hides selected columns in Excel.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + 6 (Option 1): Toggles the display of objects (shapes, charts, images) on the worksheet; unrelated to underlining text.

 

• Ctrl + 3 (Option 2): Applies or removes italic formatting, not underline.

 

• Ctrl + 2 (Option 3): Applies or removes bold formatting, not underline.

question: What is the full form of NCRB?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Crime Records Bureau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NCRB stands for National Crime Records Bureau. (राष्ट्रीय अपराध रिकॉर्ड ब्यूरो)

 

• It was set up in 1986 under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, and is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

• NCRB collects and analyses crime data defined under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Special and Local Laws (SLL), and publishes the annual "Crime in India" report.

 

• It also maintains national criminal databases, including fingerprint records, and administers the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NCRB was established based on recommendations of the National Police Commission (1977–1981) and an MHA task force (1985).

 

• Its first Director was Mr. J.C. Bakshi, appointed in 1986.

 

NOTE

 

• National Currency Records Branch (Option 1): Not a real government agency; NCRB has no role in currency records.

 

• National Capital Register Bureau (Option 2): A fictitious/incorrect expansion of the acronym.

 

• National Criminal Records Bureau (Option 3): A close but incorrect wording; the official name uses "Crime," not "Criminal."

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the bank reserves?
I. These reserves are kept partly as cash and partly in the form of financial instruments.
II. Cash Reserves Ratio are deposits which commercial banks keep with the Reserve Bank of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Banks maintain reserves partly as cash-in-hand/cash with the RBI and partly in the form of approved financial instruments (such as government securities held under SLR).

 

• Statement II is correct: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the percentage of a commercial bank's total deposits that it must compulsorily keep as reserves, in cash form, with the Reserve Bank of India. (नकद आरक्षित अनुपात — RBI के पास जमा)

 

• CRR is a quantitative monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control liquidity; raising the CRR reduces the funds banks have available for lending.

 

• This differs from the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), which banks maintain themselves in liquid assets like cash, gold, or approved government securities (not deposited with RBI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Around the exam's period, the CRR stood at 4% of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL).

 

• CRR and SLR are both quantitative tools of monetary policy, alongside the Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, and Open Market Operations (OMO).

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement I about the composition of bank reserves is also true.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement II about CRR is also true.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both statements are factually accurate.

question: In a star network, how many lines are required for connecting N nodes to the host node?
solution_text:
The correct answer is N – 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a star topology, all nodes connect through individual dedicated lines to a central hub/host node.

 

• If the host itself is counted as one of the total N nodes, then the number of peripheral (non-host) nodes needing a connection is N – 1.

 

• Each peripheral node requires exactly one dedicated line to the central host, so the total number of lines required is N – 1.

 

• This point-to-point design means the failure of one line/node does not affect the others, but failure of the central host brings down the whole network.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Star topology is one of the most widely used LAN topologies because it is easy to install, manage and troubleshoot.

 

• A fully connected mesh topology of N nodes, by contrast, would need N(N–1)/2 lines — far more cabling than a star.

 

NOTE

 

• N + 1 (Option 1): Overcounts by one; the host does not need a line to itself.

 

• N/2 (Option 2): Does not correspond to the star topology's actual connection pattern.

 

• (N/2) – 1 (Option 3): Not a valid formula for the number of connections in a star topology.

question: Which of the following comes under the part IX of the Indian constitution?
option_1: Relations between the Union and the States
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Panchayats.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part IX of the Indian Constitution (Articles 243 to 243-O) deals with "The Panchayats", inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. (भाग IX — पंचायत)

 

• It provides for a three-tier Panchayati Raj system (Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti/Block, and Zila Parishad/District) for rural local self-government.

 

• It mandates regular elections every 5 years through State Election Commissions, and reservation of seats for SC/ST and women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG), added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992, deals with Municipalities for urban local self-government.

 

• The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment, lists 29 subjects assigned to Panchayats.

 

NOTE

 

• Relations between the Union and the States (Option 1): Covered under Part XI (Articles 245–263) of the Constitution.

 

• The Scheduled and Tribal Areas (Option 2): Covered under Part X (Articles 244–244A).

 

• Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits (Option 4): Covered under Part XII (Articles 264–300A).

question: Article 2 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
option_1: Admission or establishment of new states
option_2: Alteration of areas of existing states
option_3: Alteration of names of existing states
option_4: Name and territory of the Union
solution_text:
The correct answer is Admission or establishment of new states.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 2 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new States on terms and conditions it thinks fit. (अनुच्छेद 2 — नए राज्यों का प्रवेश या स्थापना)

 

• This article deals with the addition of territory not originally part of India (external territory), unlike Article 3, which deals with internal reorganisation of existing states.

 

• It falls under Part I of the Constitution, titled "The Union and its Territory."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim's incorporation as the 22nd state of India in 1975 is often cited in relation to admission/establishment of new territory into the Union.

 

• Parliament can form new states by a simple majority, and such laws are not treated as Constitutional Amendments under Article 368.

 

NOTE

 

• Alteration of areas of existing states (Option 2): Covered under Article 3, which allows Parliament to increase or diminish the area of any existing state.

 

• Alteration of names of existing states (Option 3): Also covered under Article 3, which allows renaming of existing states.

 

• Name and territory of the Union (Option 4): Covered under Article 1, which declares India as a "Union of States" and describes its territory.

question: Which Indian freedom fighter is also known as Bismarck of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is popularly known as the "Bismarck of India" for his crucial role in the political integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union after independence, comparable to Otto von Bismarck's unification of Germany. (भारत के बिस्मार्क — सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल)

 

• He served as India's first Deputy Prime Minister and first Home Minister.

 

• He is also widely known as the "Iron Man of India" for his firm and decisive leadership.

 

• The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, the world's tallest statue, was built in his honour and inaugurated in 2018.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sardar Patel played a key role in the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928), after which he earned the title "Sardar" (leader).

 

• National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is celebrated on 31 October, his birth anniversary.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 2): Known as the "Father of the Nation," associated with non-violent resistance and the Salt March; not called the "Bismarck of India."

 

• Lal Bahadur Shastri (Option 3): India's second Prime Minister, known for the slogan "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan."

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 4): India's first Prime Minister, known as "Chacha Nehru" and architect of India's modern industrial and foreign policy.

question: Which country won the Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2022 for cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Women's T20 Asia Cup was held in Sylhet, Bangladesh, in October 2022.

 

• India defeated Sri Lanka in the final, winning by 8 wickets, to lift the trophy.

 

• This was India's 7th Women's Asia Cup T20 title, continuing their dominance in the tournament since its inception.

 

• Harmanpreet Kaur captained the Indian side to victory in this edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sri Lanka went on to break India's dominance by winning their maiden Women's Asia Cup title only in 2024, defeating India in that year's final.

 

• The Women's Asia Cup has primarily been played in the T20 format since 2016.

 

NOTE

 

• Pakistan (Option 1): Participated in the 2022 tournament but did not win the title.

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 2): Runner-up in the 2022 final; won the title for the first time only in 2024.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 3): Hosted the 2022 tournament but did not win the title.

question: What is the radius of the earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6371 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mean radius of the Earth is approximately 6,371 km. (पृथ्वी की औसत त्रिज्या ≈ 6371 किमी)

 

• Because Earth is an oblate spheroid (slightly flattened at the poles, bulging at the equator), its equatorial radius (~6,378 km) is slightly larger than its polar radius (~6,357 km); 6,371 km is the average/mean value.

 

• Earth's circumference at the equator is about 40,075 km.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Earth's oblate shape was mathematically predicted by Sir Isaac Newton based on his laws of gravitation and rotation.

 

• Earth's total surface area is about 510 million sq km, of which roughly 71% is covered by water.

 

NOTE

 

• 7456 km (Option 1): Too large; does not correspond to any standard measurement of Earth's radius.

 

• 5619 km (Option 3): Too small; not a recognised value for Earth's radius.

 

• 4728 km (Option 4): Also incorrect; does not match any standard measurement of Earth.

question: In humans the neck is joined by the head by which of the following joints?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pivotal joint.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The joint between the head (skull) and the neck that allows rotational movement (turning the head sideways, as in gesturing "no") is the pivotal (pivot) joint, formed at the atlanto-axial joint between the atlas (C1) and axis (C2) vertebrae. (धुराग्र संधि — पिवोटल जॉइंट)

 

• A pivot joint permits rotation around a single axis — one bone rotates within a ring formed by another bone and a ligament.

 

• The nodding "yes" movement of the head occurs at the atlanto-occipital joint, but the head–neck joint in this context is classified as the pivotal joint responsible for rotation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Another pivot joint in the human body is between the radius and ulna at the elbow (proximal radioulnar joint), enabling forearm rotation (pronation/supination).

 

• Types of synovial joints include ball-and-socket, hinge, pivot, saddle, condyloid (ellipsoidal), and gliding (plane) joints.

 

NOTE

 

• Ball and socket joint (Option 1): Found at the shoulder and hip; allows movement in almost all directions.

 

• Hinge joint (Option 2): Found at the elbow and knee; allows movement in one plane only, like a door hinge.

 

• Fixed joint (Option 4): Also called a fibrous/immovable joint, found between the bones of the skull (cranial sutures); allows no movement.

question:
Which of the following pairs of 'mineral – source' is correct?
I. Vitamin A – Papaya
II. Iron – Spinach
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Papaya is a rich source of Vitamin A (as beta-carotene), along with other fruits and vegetables like carrots, mangoes and pumpkins.

 

• Statement II is correct: Spinach is a well-known dietary source of Iron, along with other leafy greens and legumes. (पालक — आयरन का स्रोत)

 

• Vitamin A deficiency can cause night blindness, while Iron deficiency leads to anaemia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other good sources of iron include jaggery, pulses, and red meat; Vitamin C enhances the body's absorption of iron.

 

• Vitamin A deficiency remains a public-health concern in parts of India, addressed through supplementation programmes.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, as both statements are factually accurate.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement II (Iron–Spinach) is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement I (Vitamin A–Papaya) is also correct.

question: Who won the men’s singles title at the Australian Open 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rafael Nadal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rafael Nadal won the men's singles title at the Australian Open 2022, defeating Daniil Medvedev in a five-set final. (ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन 2022 — राफेल नडाल)

 

• With this win, Nadal became the first man in tennis history to win 21 Grand Slam singles titles, surpassing his rivals Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic (tied at 20 at the time).

 

• Nadal came back from two sets down to win the final 2–6, 6–7, 6–4, 6–4, 7–5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Australian Open 2022 women's singles title was won by Ashleigh Barty of Australia.

 

• Novak Djokovic, the defending champion, was deported from Australia before the tournament due to a visa/vaccination controversy and could not participate.

 

NOTE

 

• Casper Ruud (Option 2): A Norwegian player who reached the Australian Open final only in a later year, not in 2022.

 

• Daniil Medvedev (Option 3): The runner-up to Nadal in the 2022 final.

 

• Novak Djokovic (Option 4): The defending champion who was denied entry into Australia and could not compete in the 2022 edition.

question: As per the census of 2011, what is the annual growth rate in population of India from 2001 to 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.64 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, India's population grew from about 102.87 crore (2001) to 121.09 crore (2011), registering a decadal growth rate of 17.64%.

 

• The corresponding average annual exponential growth rate for this decade was 1.64% per annum. (2001–2011 वार्षिक वृद्धि दर — 1.64%)

 

• This represented a decline compared to the previous decade (1991–2001), which had a higher decadal growth rate of about 21.5%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence; India recorded the world's second-highest population after China.

 

• India's sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males, and the literacy rate was 74.04%.

 

NOTE

 

• 1.97 percent (Option 1): Not the correct figure for the 2001–2011 decade.

 

• 2.16 percent (Option 3): Not the correct annual growth figure for this period.

 

• 2.22 percent (Option 4): Closer to growth rates seen in earlier decades, not 2001–2011.

question: Uday Shankar was an Indian dancer best known for creating a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fusion style of dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uday Shankar (1900–1977) was a pioneering Indian dancer and choreographer, regarded as the father of modern Indian dance/ballet. (उदय शंकर — फ्यूज़न नृत्य शैली के प्रवर्तक)

 

• He is best known for creating a fusion style of dance that blended Indian classical and folk dance traditions with elements of Western ballet and theatrical technique.

 

• He founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre at Almora in 1938 to train dancers in this new form.

 

• He was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship and the Padma Vibhushan for his contribution to Indian dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• His brother, Ravi Shankar, was a legendary Indian sitar player and Bharat Ratna awardee.

 

• Uday Shankar's landmark film "Kalpana" (1948) showcased his choreography and remains a classic of Indian dance cinema.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian style of dance (Option 1): Too generic and incorrect; his innovation was specifically a fusion/hybrid style, not a purely traditional Indian style.

 

• Folk dance style (Option 3): He did not create a folk dance style; he blended classical dance and Western elements instead.

 

• American Style of dance (Option 4): Incorrect; his style was rooted in Indian tradition fused mainly with European ballet, not American dance.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "players in a team – sports" is correct?
I. 11 – basketball
II. 11 – volleyball
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is incorrect: A basketball team fields 5 players on court at a time, not 11.

 

• Statement II is incorrect: A volleyball team fields 6 players on court at a time, not 11.

 

• The number "11" corresponds to team sizes in sports like cricket, football (soccer), and hockey, not basketball or volleyball.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common on-field team sizes: Kabaddi has 7 players per side; a basketball squad may include up to 12 players, but only 5 play at a time.

 

• Volleyball rules require exactly 6 players per side on the court, rotating serve positions clockwise.

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 1): Incorrect, since neither statement about "11 players" is true for basketball or volleyball.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, because basketball has 5 players per team, not 11.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, because volleyball has 6 players per team, not 11.

question: Arid soils are characteristically developed in ________________, which exhibit characteristic arid topography.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Western Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arid soils are characteristically developed in Western Rajasthan, the region exhibiting typical arid topography (Thar Desert). (शुष्क मृदा — पश्चिमी राजस्थान)

 

• These soils are sandy in structure, saline in nature, and have low nitrogen and humus content due to sparse vegetation and low rainfall.

 

• Arid soils often have a high concentration of calcium carbonate (kankar) in their lower horizons because of high evaporation rates.

 

• With irrigation, such soils can become productive, as seen in parts of Rajasthan served by the Indira Gandhi Canal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arid soils occupy about 4.42% of India's total geographical area, mostly in Rajasthan, with smaller extents in Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana.

 

• India's other major soil types include Alluvial, Black (Regur), Red and Yellow, Laterite, and Mountain/Forest soils.

 

NOTE

 

• Southern Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Not associated with arid soils; has red/mixed soils.

 

• Western Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Predominantly fertile alluvial soils of the Indo-Gangetic plain, not arid soils.

 

• Southern Rajasthan (Option 4): Has relatively better rainfall (Aravalli region) and is not characterised by arid soils like Western Rajasthan.

question: During which of the following years did Qutbuddin Aybak rule?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1206 – 1210.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Qutbuddin Aybak, a former Turkic slave (Mamluk) of Muhammad of Ghor, founded the Delhi Sultanate (Mamluk/Slave Dynasty) in 1206 after Muhammad Ghori's death. (कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक — गुलाम वंश के संस्थापक)

 

• He ruled from 1206 to 1210, initially basing himself at Lahore before shifting focus to Delhi, and took the title of Sultan.

 

• He began construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi (completed later by his successor Iltutmish) and built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

 

• He died in 1210 from injuries sustained in a fall from his horse while playing chaugan (polo) at Lahore; he was known as "Lakh Baksh" (giver of lakhs) for his generosity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aybak was briefly succeeded by Aram Shah before Iltutmish took over and consolidated the Delhi Sultanate.

 

• The Slave Dynasty ruled Delhi from 1206 to 1290, eventually succeeded by the Khalji Dynasty.

 

NOTE

 

• 1320–1324 (Option 2): Falls under the early Tughlaq dynasty (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's reign began in 1320), unrelated to Aybak.

 

• 1290–1296 (Option 3): Corresponds to the early reign of Jalaluddin Khalji, founder of the Khalji dynasty.

 

• 1266–1287 (Option 4): Corresponds to the reign of Ghiyasuddin Balban, a later Slave dynasty ruler.

question: Kye Gompa, the largest centre of Buddhist learning in the Western Himalayas, is situated in the state/union territory of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kye Gompa (also spelt Ki/Key Monastery) is the largest Buddhist monastery/centre of learning in the Spiti Valley region of the Western Himalayas. (की गोम्पा — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It is located in the Lahaul and Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh, perched atop a hill at an altitude of about 4,166 metres.

 

• Believed to have been founded around the 11th century, it belongs to the Gelug sect of Tibetan Buddhism and serves as a training centre for lamas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Spiti Valley monasteries in Himachal Pradesh include the Tabo Monastery (one of the oldest continuously functioning monasteries in the Himalayas) and Dhankar Monastery.

 

• Himachal Pradesh is also home to important Buddhist sites such as the Dalai Lama's residence in McLeod Ganj, Dharamshala.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 1): Home to Hindu pilgrimage sites like Kedarnath and Badrinath, not to Kye Gompa.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Not associated with Buddhist monasteries of this kind; predominantly Sikh cultural heritage.

 

• Jammu & Kashmir (Option 4): Has its own Buddhist monasteries (e.g., Hemis, Thiksey, now in the UT of Ladakh), but not Kye Gompa, which is in Himachal Pradesh.

question: Which of the following combinations of ‘RBI Tool – Monetary instrument’ is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qualitative – Moral Suasion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Moral suasion is a qualitative (selective) tool of monetary policy where the RBI persuades and appeals to banks through discussions/advice to follow its monetary policy directives, without using coercive statutory means. (नैतिक दबाव — गुणात्मक साधन)

 

• Qualitative tools regulate the direction and quality of credit and include Moral Suasion, Margin Requirements, and Credit Rationing.

 

• Quantitative tools, by contrast, regulate the overall volume of credit/money supply and include CRR, SLR, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Bank Rate, and Open Market Operations (OMO).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), constituted under the RBI Act 1934 (amended 2016), decides the policy repo rate.

 

• "Margin requirement" refers to the gap between the value of security offered for a loan and the actual loan amount sanctioned; it is a qualitative tool.

 

NOTE

 

• Quantitative – Marginal requirement (Option 2): Incorrect pairing; margin requirement is a qualitative, not quantitative, tool.

 

• Qualitative - Cash Reserve ratio (Option 3): Incorrect pairing; CRR is a quantitative tool, not qualitative.

 

• Qualitative – Open Market Operations (Option 4): Incorrect pairing; OMO is a quantitative tool, not qualitative.

question: Who was the Governor General of Bengal when the Permanent Settlement was introduced there in 1793?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Charles Cornwallis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Charles Cornwallis, as Governor-General of Bengal, introduced the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) in 1793, primarily in the provinces of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. (स्थायी बंदोबस्त 1793 — लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस)

 

• Under this system, zamindars were recognised as hereditary owners of land and made responsible for collecting revenue from peasants, paying a fixed amount to the East India Company in perpetuity.

 

• Cornwallis also reformed the civil services and judiciary in British India, and is known for his defeat against Tipu Sultan in the Third Anglo-Mysore War (Treaty of Seringapatam, 1792).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Permanent Settlement fixed the government's revenue demand forever, giving the Company certainty of income while zamindars bore the risk of famine/crop failure.

 

• Later revenue systems introduced elsewhere in India included the Ryotwari System (Madras and Bombay presidencies) and the Mahalwari System (parts of North India).

 

NOTE

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 2): Governor-General known for social reforms, including abolition of Sati (1829) and suppression of Thuggee.

 

• Lord Mountbatten (Option 3): The last Viceroy of British India, who oversaw Partition and Independence in 1947.

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 4): Known as the "Father of Local Self-Government" in India; introduced the Ripon Resolution of 1882.

question:
Which of the following pairs of 'number – composition' is correct?
I. Atomic number – number of protons
II. Mass number – Sum of number of neutrons and protons
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: The atomic number (Z) of an element is defined as the number of protons present in the nucleus of its atom.

 

• Statement II is correct: The mass number (A) of an element is defined as the sum of the number of protons and neutrons (collectively called nucleons) in its nucleus. (द्रव्यमान संख्या — प्रोटॉन + न्यूट्रॉन)

 

• These two quantities, along with the number of electrons (equal to protons in a neutral atom), define the identity and isotopic form of an element.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same atomic number) with different numbers of neutrons, and hence different mass numbers.

 

• The atomic number of an element determines its position in the Modern Periodic Table, arranged as per Henry Moseley's Law.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since Statement II about mass number is also correct.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, as both statements are accurate definitions.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incomplete, since Statement I about atomic number is also correct.

question: Who has made history by becoming the first woman vice president of the United States of America?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamala Harris.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kamala Harris made history by becoming the first woman, first Black American, and first person of South Asian (Indian) descent to become Vice President of the United States, taking office on 20 January 2021. (कमला हैरिस — अमेरिका की पहली महिला उपराष्ट्रपति)

 

• She served alongside President Joe Biden as the 49th Vice President of the United States.

 

• Prior to this, she served as a U.S. Senator from California and as California's Attorney General.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kamala Harris's mother, Shyamala Gopalan, was an Indian-American cancer researcher, reflecting her partial Indian heritage.

 

• Around the period of this exam, she remained the sitting Vice President of the United States under the Biden administration.

 

NOTE

 

• Marguerite Higgins (Option 1): An American journalist and war correspondent, noted for her Pulitzer Prize-winning coverage of the Korean War; unrelated to the vice presidency.

 

• Eleanor Roosevelt (Option 2): Wife of President Franklin D. Roosevelt and a noted human-rights advocate/First Lady, not a Vice President.

 

• Suchitra Pal (Option 3): Not linked to the office of U.S. Vice President; not a historically recognised figure in this context.

question: Which of the following is an endemic species?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nicobar pigeon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nicobar pigeon (*Caloenas nicobarica*) is classified, in standard Indian conservation/exam references, as an endemic species of India, being largely restricted to the Nicobar Islands and adjoining small islands of the Andaman & Nicobar archipelago. (निकोबर कबूतर — स्थानिक प्रजाति)

 

• Endemic species are those confined to a specific geographic area/habitat and not found naturally anywhere else.

 

• The Nicobar pigeon is a protected species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and is categorised as "Near Threatened" by the IUCN.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable endemic species of India include the Asiatic lion (Gir forest, Gujarat), Nilgiri tahr (Western Ghats), Sangai deer (Manipur), and the Purple frog (Western Ghats).

 

• India has four recognised biodiversity hotspots, including the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, known for their high degree of endemism.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian wild ass (Option 2): Found in India (notably the Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat), but standard exam classification of India's "endemic species" places the Nicobar pigeon in this category rather than the Indian wild ass here.

 

• Desert fox (Option 3): Found across arid regions of India, Pakistan, Iran and North Africa; not endemic to India.

 

• Indian rhino (Option 4): Found in India and Nepal (Terai grasslands and floodplains); its range extends beyond India alone.

question: Who has won the Miss India Worldwide 2022 pageant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khushi Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khushi Patel, representing the United Kingdom, won the title of Miss India Worldwide 2022. (मिस इंडिया वर्ल्डवाइड 2022 — खुशी पटेल)

 

• The pageant celebrates the global Indian diaspora, with contestants of Indian origin from various countries competing for the crown.

 

• The event, organised by the Indasia Entertainment Group, was held in the United States in June 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Miss India Worldwide is distinct from the Femina Miss India and Miss Diva pageants held within India for the Miss World and Miss Universe franchises respectively.

 

• It specifically recognises and celebrates women of Indian origin/heritage living outside India.

 

NOTE

 

• Roshani Razack (Option 2): A pageant contestant of Indian-diaspora heritage, but not the winner of the 2022 edition of Miss India Worldwide.

 

• Vaidehi Dongre (Option 3): Associated with a different Indian-American pageant title around this period, not Miss India Worldwide 2022.

 

• Navya Paingol (Option 4): Not the winner of the Miss India Worldwide 2022 pageant.
